A **p-value statistic** is a statistic $p:\mathcal X\to[0,1]$, where $[0,1]$ carries the trace of the Borel sigma-algebra, meaning
$\{B\cap[0,1]:B\in\mathcal B(\mathbb R)\}$
([[def-statistic-and-estimator]],
[[def-measurable-function-between-measurable-spaces]]).

A **statistic** with target measurable space $(\mathcal Y,\mathcal B)$ is a measurable map
$T:(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)\to(\mathcal Y,\mathcal B)$, where measurability
means that $T^{-1}(B)\in\mathcal A$ for every $B\in\mathcal B$
([[def-measurable-function-between-measurable-spaces]]).

Given $\alpha\in[0,1]$ and an observation $x\in\mathcal X$, order the indices by the pairs $(p_i(x),i)$ in lexicographic order. This gives a unique permutation $\pi$ with $p_{\pi(1)}(x)\le\cdots\le p_{\pi(m)}(x)$; ties are ordered by increasing index.

A function $f : X \to Y$ is **measurable** when

$$f^{-1}(B) \in \mathcal{A} \qquad \text{for every } B \in \mathcal{B}.$$

Let $X$ be a set. A **sigma-algebra on $X$** is an algebra of subsets

For each $i\in[m]$, let $p_i:\mathcal X\to[0,1]$ be a p-value statistic ([[def-p-value]]). It is **valid for $H_{0i}$** when

$$P_\theta\{x:p_i(x)\le u\}\le u\qquad(\theta\in H_{0i},\ 0\le u\le1).$$

For $\theta\in\Theta$, the **true-null index set** is
$$I_0(\theta):=\{i\in[m]:\theta\in H_{0i}\}.$$

The rejected-index set is $R_\alpha(x)=\{\pi(j):1\le j\le r_\alpha(x)\}$. Reject $H_{0i}$ exactly when $i\in R_\alpha(x)$; equivalently, compare sequentially to $\alpha/(m-j+1)$, stop at the first failed comparison, and reject only the preceding ranks.
For the rejected-index set $R_\alpha(x)$ from [[alg-holm-step-down-procedure]], each rejection event $D_i(\alpha):=\{x\in\mathcal X:i\in R_\alpha(x)\}$ belongs to $\mathcal A$.

For $\alpha\in[0,1]$, reject $H_{0i}$ exactly when $p_i(X)\le\alpha/m$. Then, for every $\theta$ in the parameter space,
$$P_\theta\{\text{at least one true null is rejected}\}=P_\theta(V_\theta\ge1)\le\alpha.$$ 
The bound holds for every true-null configuration, including the global null and configurations with false nulls, and for arbitrary dependence among the p-values.

derivations.claim: For m_0>0, any Holm rejection of a true null forces rejection of the earliest-ranked true null. Its rank j_0 satisfies m-j_0+1≥m_0, so its rejected p-value is at most α/m_0. The Holm false-rejection event is therefore contained in the union of the m_0 true-null events {p_i(X)≤α/m_0}.

For fixed θ with m_0>0, the true-null subfamily has m_0 members and all are true under θ. Applying the Bonferroni theorem with cutoff α/m_0 bounds the probability of its union of threshold events by α. The Holm error event is a subset of this union.
